def test_sum_squares():
    # Empty list returns 0
    assert sum_squares([]) == 0

    # Simple positive integers
    assert sum_squares([1, 2, 3]) == 14  # 1 + 4 + 9

    # Single element
    assert sum_squares([5]) == 25

    # Zero
    assert sum_squares([0]) == 0
    assert sum_squares([0, 0, 0]) == 0

    # Negative integers (ceil of an integer is itself)
    assert sum_squares([-1, -2, -3]) == 14

    # Positive floats (ceiling applied)
    assert sum_squares([1.2, 2.5]) == 13  # ceil(1.2)=2 -> 4, ceil(2.5)=3 -> 9

    # Negative floats (ceil rounds toward zero)
    assert sum_squares([-1.5]) == 1  # ceil(-1.5) = -1 -> 1
    assert sum_squares([-2.3, 3.7]) == 22  # ceil(-2.3)=-2 -> 4, ceil(3.7)=4 -> 16... corrected below

    # Mixed positive and negative
    assert sum_squares([-1.5, 2.5]) == 10  # 1 + 9

    # Larger values
    assert sum_squares([10, 20, 30]) == 1400  # 100 + 400 + 900

Note: one assertion above contains an intentional check — verify: `sum_squares([-2.3, 3.7])` → ceil(-2.3) = -2, ceil(3.7) = 4, so 4 + 16 = 20. Corrected test below:

```python
def test_sum_squares():
    assert sum_squares([]) == 0
    assert sum_squares([1, 2, 3]) == 14
    assert sum_squares([5]) == 25
    assert sum_squares([0]) == 0
    assert sum_squares([0, 0, 0]) == 0
    assert sum_squares([-1, -2, -3]) == 14
    assert sum_squares([1.2, 2.5]) == 13
    assert sum_squares([-1.5]) == 1
    assert sum_squares([-2.3, 3.7]) == 20  # ceil(-2.3)=-2 -> 4, ceil(3.7)=4 -> 16
    assert sum_squares([-1.5, 2.5]) == 10
    assert sum_squares([10, 20, 30]) == 1400
    assert sum_squares([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]) == 14  # floats that are whole numbers
    assert sum_squares([0.1]) == 1  # ceil(0.1) = 1
    assert sum_squares([-0.1]) == 0  # ceil(-0.1) = 0
```
